newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt minister welcomes militant truce call.
newsitem.headline: Egypt minister welcomes militant truce call.

text.p: Egyptian Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi on Monday welcomed a call for a truce by a group of imprisoned Moslem militant leaders, in an apparent change in his stance towards the appeal for an end to violence.

Asked to comment on a report in an international newspaper that Sheikh Omar Abdel Rahman, the Egyptian cleric jailed for life in the U.S. for plotting to bomb New York landmarks, had supported the call, Alfi told reporters:

"Our main goal, as a security body, is to create a favourable atmosphere to attract investment and tourists. Therefore, we welcome any initiative that includes statements or actions which support this goal."
The London-based al-Hayat newspaper last week quoted Sheikh Omar Abdel-Rahman's lawyer as saying the cleric had issued a statement from his cell supporting the call for a truce.
Six imprisoned leaders of the militant al-Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) issued a statement last month calling on their followers to stop unilaterally all violent acts.
Alfi described the truce in July as a ruse intended to improve the militants' public image.

"These groups felt the people were against them and they are trying to win over public opinion by calling for this ceasefire. They want to make the people sympathetic to their activities that contravene Islam. This is a manoeuvre," Alfi said in July.

The appeal, read out by an alleged militant at a trial last month, was rejected by exiled Gama'a leaders who said they would continue their armed struggle to transform Egypt into a strict Moslem state.
More than 1,000 people have been killed since the group took up arms in 1992 to overthrow the government and transform Egypt into a strict Islamic state.

Police say they have broken the back of the military wing of the Gama'a through crackdowns and the number of attacks has declined sharply since the mid-1990s, when the militants were killing about one policeman a day.
